questionText:
A lexical analyzer uses the following patterns to recognize three tokens $T_1, T_2$, and $T_3$ over the alphabet $\{a,b,c\}$.

$$T_1: a?(b|c)^*a$$
$$T_2: b?(a|c)^*b$$
$$T_3: c?(b|a)^*c$$

Note that ‘$x?$’ means 0 or 1 occurrence of the symbol $x$. Note also that the analyzer outputs the token that matches the longest possible prefix.

If the string $bbaacabc$ is processed by the analyzer, which one of the following is the sequence of tokens it outputs?
explanation:
To determine the sequence of tokens output by the lexical analyzer, we use the longest prefix matching rule on the input string $bbaacabc$.

1. First Token Matching (Input: $bbaacabc$)
• $T_1 = a?(b|c)^*a$: Matches $bba$ (length 3).
• $T_2 = b?(a|c)^*b$: Matches $bb$ (length 2).
• $T_3 = c?(b|a)^*c$: Matches $bbaac$ (length 5).
The longest matching prefix is $bbaac$ of length 5, which corresponds to token $T_3$.

2. Second Token Matching (Remaining Input: $abc$)
• $T_1 = a?(b|c)^*a$: No valid match.
• $T_2 = b?(a|c)^*b$: Matches $ab$ (length 2).
• $T_3 = c?(b|a)^*c$: Matches $abc$ (length 3).
The longest matching prefix is $abc$ of length 3, which corresponds to token $T_3$.

Thus, the sequence of tokens output is $T_3T_3$.
